# Coursera DL — Full Documentation

> Extended technical documentation, architecture, feature breakdown, and build instructions for Coursera DL.

## Overview
Coursera DL is an open-source desktop application that enables users to preserve enrolled Coursera learning materials locally for offline study. It is built using Tauri v2, a Rust backend, and a React frontend.

## Key Features
- **Video Downloads**: Download 720p and 1080p MP4 lectures with localized subtitles (.vtt).
- **Course Assets**: Archive lecture notes, readings, supplemental resources, and assignment assets.
- **Specialization Support**: Batch enroll and batch archive all nested modules across complete specializations.
- **Privacy & Security**: Authentication takes place strictly on the client using session cookies (`CAUTH`). No credentials or personal telemetry are sent to external servers.

## Quick Start
1. Log in to Coursera in your web browser.
2. Export your session cookie (`CAUTH`).
3. Open Coursera DL and enter your cookie.
4. Select courses and target directory to start archiving.

## Development & Build
- Prerequisites: Node.js (>=18), Rust toolchain (cargo), and pnpm.
- Clone: `git clone https://github.com/courseradl/coursera-dl-gui.git`
- Run Dev: `pnpm install && pnpm tauri dev`
- Build: `pnpm tauri build`
